recognize_zh: 箭頭所指兩個紅血球淡染（低色素），細胞質中佈滿大小不一的藍色點狀顆粒，即嗜鹼性點彩（basophilic stippling）；背景有許多標靶細胞與低色素小紅血球，提示血紅素疾病（如地中海型貧血）。
features: Two pale, hypochromic RBCs (arrows) with fine-to-coarse blue punctate granules evenly distributed through the cell (basophilic stippling)
Numerous target cells (codocytes) in the background
Hypochromic microcytes and occasional teardrop/irregular poikilocytes
RBC with a central refractile inclusion-like body (likely artifact/overlying platelet)
Scattered platelets; no leukocytes in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked poikilocytosis with numerous target cells and hypochromic microcytes. Two pale red cells contain numerous fine to coarse, evenly distributed basophilic granules consistent with basophilic stippling, representing aggregated ribosomal RNA. Scattered platelets are present. Findings of basophilic stippling with prominent target cells and hypochromia are suggestive of a hemoglobin disorder such as thalassemia; lead poisoning and pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency are other causes to consider, and hemoglobin analysis and lead level are recommended as appropriate.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are few small clustered granules at the cell periphery and stain with Prussian blue, whereas stippling is numerous and diffusely distributed.
A Howell-Jolly body is a single larger round dense DNA remnant rather than many fine blue dots.
Polychromatophilic cells have uniform bluish-gray tint without discrete granules on Wright stain.
Parasites show ring structures with chromatin dots and cytoplasm, not diffuse punctate dots.
